questions.question_text: The highly polished life-size sculpture of the 'Chauri Bearer' (Yakshini) discovered at Didarganj belongs to which major historical period?

sections.section_name: Section B - Art Elements & Conceptual Terms

questions.question_text: Explain the meaning and structural importance of 'Pramanam' as a core component within the Six Limbs of Indian Painting (Shadang). [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Pramanam translates to precise proportion, measure, and structural structure. It is vital as it dictates the accurate scale, anatomical ratios, and spatial relationships necessary for achieving visual harmony.

questions.question_text: Describe the conceptual role of 'Bhava' in traditional Indian aesthetics as outlined in the Shadang principles. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Bhava represents the emotion, mood, or inner feeling conveyed by an artwork. It breathes life into the visual form, establishing a deep psychological and emotional connection with the viewer.

questions.question_text: Define the element of 'Line' (Rekha) and its specific expressive function in the Ajanta mural painting tradition. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A line is a continuous mark made on a surface. In Ajanta murals, lyrical, sweeping, and rhythmic lines define volume, contour, and delicate emotional expressions without relying on heavy shading.

questions.question_text: Explain the visual element of 'Texture' in the context of sculptural art. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Texture refers to the actual tactile surface quality of an artwork. In sculpture, it describes how rough, smooth, or polished a surface feels, significantly enhancing the object's physical realism.

questions.question_text: How does the principle of 'Balance' function in a two-dimensional artistic composition? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Balance is the even distribution of visual weight across a composition. Symmetrical or asymmetrical balance ensures structural stability, preventing the artwork from feeling heavy or lopsided to the viewer.

questions.question_text: Deconstruct the stylistic modeling, posture dynamics, and aesthetic features of the famous copper-alloy 'Dancing Girl' from Mohenjo-Daro. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: This 4-inch bronze figurine displays a stylized, elongated tubular form with slightly disproportionate limbs. Standing in a relaxed, confident 'tribhanga' (triple-bent) posture with one hand on her hip, she wears heavy bangles on her left arm, reflecting dynamic liveliness and advanced lost-wax casting expertise.

questions.question_text: Analyze the aesthetic characteristics, thematic expression, and coloring techniques of the 'Bodhisattva Padmapani' mural found in Cave 1 of Ajanta. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The Bodhisattva Padmapani mural portrays the compassionate deity holding a blue lotus. It features graceful, rhythmic outlines, gentle tonal shading creating three-dimensional volume, and a downward gaze expressing immense spiritual tranquility. The tempera application utilizes natural mineral colors, highlighting early Indian classical mastery.

questions.question_text: Describe the structural execution, physical features, and hallmark finishing of the Mauryan period 'Didarganj Yakshini' (Chauri Bearer) sculpture. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Carved from a single piece of Chunar sandstone, the life-size Yakshini embodies the ancient Indian feminine ideal with full breasts, a narrow waist, and broad hips. She holds a fly-whisk (chauri) and exhibits the signature, highly lustrous Mauryan polish, demonstrating exquisite monumental stone carving skills.
